title: Nature and the Environment
description: Ten short stories about nature and the environment: a bus trip to a national park, a winter bird count, a community garden, a school battery project, ice fishing, a mountain walk, a lake cleanup, a nature writer, bees in a village and a candidate who wants better buses.

lessons.title: The Bus to Blue Lake
lessons.summary: Daniel and his daughter take a bus to a national park to see the mountains and the horses.
lessons.text:
Daniel lived in a big city with his daughter, Mia. Mia was 10 years old, and she loved animals. One night, Daniel was reading a book when Mia came into the room.

"Dad, I have never seen a real mountain," she said. "And I have never seen a horse. Can we go somewhere with mountains and horses?"

"That's a good idea," Daniel said. "Let's decide where to go." It was not hard to decide. Blue Lake National Park was 3 hours from the city, and it had high mountains, a big lake and wild horses.

Daniel didn't have a car, so he looked at the bus schedule on his phone. The schedule said that a bus left the city at 7 in the morning and arrived at the park at 10. Another bus left the park at 5 and came back to the city at 8. Daniel bought 2 tickets online. His ticket was $15, and Mia's ticket was $8.

On Saturday, they got on the bus at 7. There was a lot of traffic in the city, but the driver wasn't worried. "It will be faster after we leave the city," he said. He was right. Soon the bus was driving between green hills, and Mia was looking at the mountains through the window.

At the park, they met a guide named Ruth. "I have worked in this park for 20 years," the guide told them. "What do you want to see?"

"Horses!" Mia said.

"Then I recommend a walk along the lake," the guide said. "The horses usually come to the water in the morning. I also recommend the small hill near the lake. The view from the top is the best view in the park."

Daniel and Mia walked along the lake, and soon they saw 6 horses. The horses were drinking water from the lake. Mia took a lot of photos. Then they walked up the small hill. From the top, they could see the mountains, the lake and the horses.

"This is the most beautiful place in the world," Mia said.

At 5, they got on the bus back to the city. Mia was tired and happy, and she slept all the way home.

Questions:
Why did Daniel and Mia go to the national park?
They went because Mia wanted to see a real mountain and a horse.
Why did they travel by bus?
They traveled by bus because Daniel didn't have a car.
How much were the tickets?
Daniel's ticket was $15, and Mia's ticket was $8.
What did the guide recommend?
The guide recommended a walk along the lake and the view from the small hill.
What were the horses doing when Daniel and Mia saw them?
The horses were drinking water from the lake.

lessons.title: The Winter Bird Count
lessons.summary: A man who has watched birds for 40 years does the town's winter bird count with a phone app.
lessons.text:
My name is Walter. I am 68 years old, and I have watched birds for more than 40 years. Every winter, our town has a bird count. On one day in January, people go out and count all the birds that they see. Then they send the numbers to a national bird organization, which uses them to learn about the birds in our state.

For many years, I wrote my numbers on paper. This winter, my grandson Eric showed me an app for my phone. "Your phone is a great device for the bird count," he said. "The app is very basic. You will learn it in 5 minutes."

He was right. The app is basic, and it is easy to use. First, you click "Start." Then the app locates you on a map, so you don't have to write where you are. When you see a bird, you select its name from a list. Then you enter the number. If you see multiple birds of the same kind, you don't have to count every bird. You can estimate the number.

On the day of the count, Eric and I went to the lake at 7 in the morning. Birds are most active early in the morning, when they are looking for food. It was very cold, but the birds were active. We saw multiple kinds of birds: small brown birds in the trees, black birds on the ground and big white birds on the water.

The big white birds were the hardest to count, because there were so many of them. "How many do you think?" Eric asked. "I estimate 200," I said. I selected their name on the list and clicked 200. The app located us again, near the north end of the lake.

In 3 hours, we selected 14 kinds of birds. My old paper lists never had more than 10. "The device is better than my paper," I told Eric. He laughed.

That night, I clicked "Send." I am already waiting for next winter.

Questions:
How long has Walter watched birds?
He has watched birds for more than 40 years.
Who showed Walter the app?
His grandson Eric showed him the app.
What does the app do after you click "Start"?
The app locates you on a map.
Why did they go to the lake early in the morning?
They went early because birds are most active early in the morning.
How many big white birds did Walter estimate?
He estimated 200 big white birds.

lessons.title: The Garden on Elm Street
lessons.summary: An old woman and her neighbors turn an empty piece of land into a community garden.
lessons.text:
Rosa has lived on Elm Street for 50 years. Next to her building, there used to be a square piece of empty land. For a long time, it was full of old chairs, broken boxes and other waste. None of the people on the street liked it, but none of them did anything about it.

One spring, Rosa decided to change that. She went to the city office and asked, "Can we make a garden on the empty land next to my building?" The city said yes.

Rosa wrote a note and put it on every door on the street: "Do you want a community garden? Come to the empty land next to my building on Saturday at 10." She wasn't sure that anyone would come. But the news spread quickly. On Saturday, 25 people came. There were children, parents and grandparents: 3 generations of people from the same street.

First, they took out the broken boxes and the other waste. They kept 4 old chairs that were still good. Then they made 12 small square gardens, one for each family. Each square garden was 10 feet by 10 feet. The older generation knew a lot about growing food and flowers. The younger generation was strong and fast. So they worked well together.

Rosa planted roses, because roses were her mother's favorite flower. A young man called Kofi planted food for his family. 2 children planted big yellow flowers that grow very tall.

All summer, the garden was growing. People came every evening to give water to their plants and to talk. The roses spread along the wall. Kofi cleaned the 4 old chairs and put them under a tree. Now the chairs were not waste anymore. They were a place to sit and rest.

In September, the people of Elm Street had a party in the garden. Rosa stood next to her roses and said, "Last year, this place was full of waste. Look at what we have achieved together." Everyone agreed. In one summer, they achieved a lot.

Questions:
What was next to Rosa's building before the garden?
There was a square piece of empty land, full of old chairs, broken boxes and other waste.
How many people came on Saturday?
25 people came, from 3 generations.
Why did the older and the younger generations work well together?
The older generation knew a lot about growing food and flowers, and the younger generation was strong and fast.
Why did Rosa plant roses?
She planted roses because roses were her mother's favorite flower.
What did Kofi do with the old chairs?
He cleaned them and put them under a tree.

lessons.title: The Battery Box
lessons.summary: A school principal and her students collect old batteries in the library to help the environment.
lessons.text:
Ms. Lopez is the principal of Oak Hill Elementary School. Every month, she has a short session with the fourth grade students about the environment. In one session, a student called Ben asked a question. "What happens to old batteries?"

"That is a very good question," the principal said. "Many people put old batteries in the trash with other waste. But batteries have things inside them that are bad for the environment. They can go into the ground and into the water."

"Then we should collect them," Ben said.

The principal liked the idea. "OK," she said. "The library will be our battery center." The next day, the students put a big box in the school library. They wrote on it: "Battery Box. Bring your old batteries here!"

The box was strong, but it could hold a maximum of 40 pounds. "40 pounds is the maximum," the principal told the students. "When the box is full, it is necessary to take it to the city waste center. They know how to make old batteries safe."

The students also needed a scale. Ben brought a small scale from home. Every Friday, 2 students put the box on the scale and wrote down the number of pounds.

At first, the box was almost empty. After the first week, the scale said 3 pounds. But the students made signs and talked about the box in every class. Soon parents and teachers were bringing batteries too. After the fourth week, the scale said 38 pounds, almost the maximum.

The principal drove the box to the city waste center. A man there put it on a bigger scale. "38 pounds," he said. "That is a lot of batteries. Your project has been very successful."

At the next session, the principal had good news. "Our project was successful," she said, "so the Battery Box is going to stay in the library. It is necessary for our environment."

Questions:
Who is Ms. Lopez?
Ms. Lopez is the principal of Oak Hill Elementary School.
Why are old batteries bad for the environment?
They have things inside them that can go into the ground and into the water.
What was the maximum that the box could hold?
The box could hold a maximum of 40 pounds.
What did the students do every Friday?
They put the box on the scale and wrote down the number of pounds.
Why is the Battery Box going to stay in the library?
It is going to stay because the project was successful.

lessons.title: Ice Fishing with Dad
lessons.summary: In her diary, a girl writes about waiting for the ice on the lake to be firm enough for ice fishing.
lessons.text:
Monday, January 8

Dad and I are staying in a small house next to a lake this week. Dad has promised to take me ice fishing. Today the surface of the lake was white, but Dad said that the ice wasn't firm yet. "It isn't strong enough to hold a person," he said. "We have to wait." I wasn't happy, but I know that he is right.

Tuesday, January 9

Yesterday the wind started to blow, and it blew all night. It is still blowing today. It is very cold. Dad says that the cold wind is good news, because it will make the ice firmer. Clearly, we can't go out today, so I am reading by the fire.

Wednesday, January 10

The wind isn't blowing anymore, and the day is clear and cold. This morning, Dad walked out on the ice and made a small opening in the surface. He measured the ice. "It's firm now," he said. "It's clearly strong enough. We can go out tomorrow." I was so happy that I couldn't sit still anymore.

Thursday, January 11

Today we went ice fishing! Dad takes the ice very seriously. He told me to stay behind him, and he walked first. "If you hear a sound from the ice, stop and call me," he said. He was speaking very seriously, so I listened.

We made 2 small openings in the ice and put our lines into the water. For 2 hours, we had no luck. "That's fishing," Dad said. "Sometimes you have luck, and sometimes you don't. We'll have a good time anyway."

Then, at 11, I felt something pull on my line. It was a fish! I had some trouble with it, because it was big and strong, but Dad helped me. After that, our luck was better. We took 4 fish home, and Dad cooked them that night.

Friday, January 12

Yesterday was the best day of the week. Dad says that I had no trouble at all with my big fish. That is not true, but I am happy anyway. Next winter, we are going to come back, and I will catch a bigger fish.

Questions:
Why couldn't they go fishing on Monday?
They couldn't go because the ice wasn't firm yet.
What was the wind doing on Tuesday?
The wind was blowing, and it was very cold.
Why did Dad say the cold wind was good news?
He said it was good news because the cold wind would make the ice firmer.
Who walked first on the ice?
Dad walked first, because he takes the ice very seriously.
How many fish did they take home?
They took 4 fish home, and Dad cooked them that night.

lessons.title: An E-mail from Pine Valley
lessons.summary: In an e-mail to his sister, Jake writes about the mistake that gave him an arm injury on a mountain walk.
lessons.text:
Hi Sara,

I'm writing from my hotel in Pine Valley. I was supposed to come home on Sunday, but I am going to stay 2 more days. Don't worry: I'm OK. But I have an injury, and I want to tell you about it before Mom hears the story from someone else.

On Friday, I went for a long walk in the mountains. I am in good physical shape, so I assumed that the walk would be easy for me. That was my first mistake. The way to the top was much harder than I thought. My second mistake was the time. I started at 2 in the afternoon, but I was supposed to start in the morning, like everyone else.

At 5, I was still walking up. I was tired, and it was getting dark. I was looking at my phone when I fell on some rocks. I fell on my left arm, and it hurt a lot. I admit that I was scared.

Then a man and a woman came down the mountain. The woman was a doctor! She gave me first aid. The first aid was very basic: she put my arm in a piece of cloth so I couldn't move it. But it really helped. Then they helped me walk down. It was a struggle. It took us 2 hours, and I had to stop many times. They were very kind to me.

At the bottom, they drove me directly to the hospital. The doctor at the hospital said that the injury wasn't serious, but my arm was broken. Now I have a white cast on my arm. I have to wear the cast for 6 weeks.

I admit that it was all my mistake. I assumed that physical strength was enough. It isn't. Next time, I will start early and go with a friend.

Please tell Mom that I am fine. I am still struggling to type with one hand, so I'll call her directly tomorrow.

Love,
Jake

Questions:
Why is Jake staying in Pine Valley for 2 more days?
He is staying because he has an injury.
What did Jake assume about the walk?
He assumed that the walk would be easy, because he is in good physical shape.
What were Jake's 2 mistakes?
He assumed the walk would be easy, and he started too late in the day.
Who gave Jake first aid?
A woman who was a doctor gave him first aid.
What does Jake have on his arm now?
He has a white cast on his arm, and he has to wear it for 6 weeks.

lessons.title: Clean Lake Day
lessons.summary: The city's parks division conducts a lake cleanup, and a high school team helps.
lessons.text:
Every April, the parks division of Riverside conducts Clean Lake Day at Stone Lake. The parks division is a small part of the city administration, and it takes care of all the parks in the city. This year, a woman called Grace was in charge of Clean Lake Day. It was her first year at the parks division, and she wanted the day to be a success.

At 8 in the morning, about 60 people came to the lake. One of them was Leo, the captain of the high school football team. Leo was a good captain, and he brought his whole team with him.

Grace gave everyone gloves and a big bag. "Today we are going to collect all the waste around the lake," she said. "Please be careful near the water, because the stones are wet."

Stone Lake has a lot of stones on its shore. There are small stones, big stones and very old stones. That is why it is called Stone Lake. Unfortunately, people leave a lot of waste between the stones.

The football team collected waste along the north side of the lake. Leo was a strong captain: he worked harder than anyone, and the other players followed him. Other people collected waste near the parking lot and the picnic tables. A park guard drove a small truck around the lake and collected the full bags.

At 12, they finished. The guard put all the bags on a big scale. "The total is 450 pounds," he said. "That's more than last year."

"Overall, I am very happy," Grace said. "The city administration will be happy too." Then she thanked the football team. "Your captain told me that you finished the north side first. Thank you."

After that, everyone had something to eat by the lake. The water was clear, and the stones were clean. Overall, it was a great day for Stone Lake.

Questions:
Who conducts Clean Lake Day at Stone Lake every April?
The parks division of the city conducts it.
Who was Leo?
Leo was the captain of the high school football team.
Why is the lake called Stone Lake?
It is called Stone Lake because it has a lot of stones on its shore.
What did the park guard do?
He drove a small truck around the lake and collected the full bags.
How many pounds of waste did they collect?
They collected 450 pounds of waste.

lessons.title: A Writer in the Town Hall
lessons.summary: A teenager goes with her mother to hear a nature writer speak at the town hall, and she likes it more than she expected.
lessons.text:
My name is Emily, and I am 15 years old. Last Thursday, my mom took me to the town hall to hear a writer called Helen Brooks. She writes books about nature, and my mom has read all of them. I didn't want to go. I thought that a talk about nature would be boring.

The hall was full. There were literally no empty seats, so we had to stand at the back of the hall. I was literally the youngest person there. The writer was a small woman with white hair, and she had a lot of energy.

She started with a joke. "My friends always ask me why I don't live in the city," she said. "I tell them that I get lost in the city. In the forest, I always know where I am." Everyone laughed. It was a good joke, and after that I started to listen.

The writer talked about her life. When she was young, she used to work in an office in a big city. "I had a good job," she said, "but my soul was tired. Then one summer, I spent a month in the mountains, and my spirit came back to life."

She argued that people need nature for their soul and their spirit, not just for their bodies. "Some people argue that nature is only a nice place for a weekend," she said. "But in reality, we are part of nature. We need it every day. Thus, we must take care of it."

It was the first time that I heard the word "thus." My mom told me later that it means "so." She also said, "Trees clean the air. Thus, a city with more trees is a better city."

At the end, she read from her new book. It was about a winter in a small house in the woods. It was the best part of the evening.

On the way home, I told my mom, "That was awesome. I thought it would be boring, but the reality was very different." She was surprised. Then she laughed and gave me the writer's new book. I have already read half of it. It really is awesome.

Questions:
Why didn't Emily want to go to the talk?
She thought that a talk about nature would be boring.
Why did they have to stand at the back of the hall?
There were literally no empty seats.
What was the writer's joke about?
Her joke was about getting lost in the city.
What did the writer argue?
She argued that people need nature for their soul and their spirit, not just for their bodies.
What does "thus" mean?
"Thus" means "so."

lessons.title: Bees in the Village
lessons.summary: A young man borrows money to keep bees in his village and sells the honey at the market.
lessons.text:
Tom lives in Green Valley, a small village in the hills. For many years, the village had a farm economy: people grew food and sold it in the city. But when Tom was growing up, many families left the village. The village economy was getting worse.

Tom wanted to stay. He loved the hills, the flowers and the simple life. He wanted to keep bees and sell honey. But he needed money for bee boxes and the bees. So he went to the bank in the next town and asked for a loan.

"A loan of $5,000 is possible," the woman at the bank said. "But you will need insurance for the bees. If something happens to them, the insurance will pay." So Tom got a loan and bought insurance.

In May, Tom put 10 bee boxes in a field of flowers. In every box, there was a queen bee. The queen is the most important bee, because she is the mother of all the bees in the box. Tom checked every queen often. When the queen is well, the whole box is well.

In the first year, Tom sold his honey at the village market every Saturday. Most people paid in cash. Some people didn't have cash, so they offered to exchange. A woman from a farm exchanged a box of eggs for some honey. Tom was happy with every exchange.

At the end of the year, Tom looked at his balance at the bank. After he paid for the loan and the insurance, he had a small profit: $900. It wasn't a big profit, but it was a start.

The next year, Tom had 20 boxes and a bigger profit. He also found a good balance between work and rest. He worked hard in summer and rested in winter. Now 2 other young people in the village are keeping bees too. Little by little, the village economy is getting stronger.

Questions:
Why did Tom need a loan?
He needed money for bee boxes and the bees.
Why did Tom need insurance?
If something happened to the bees, the insurance would pay.
Why is the queen the most important bee?
She is the most important bee because she is the mother of all the bees in the box.
What did a woman from a farm exchange for some honey?
A woman from a farm exchanged a box of eggs for some honey.
How much profit did Tom have at the end of the first year?
He had a small profit of $900.

lessons.title: The Candidate Who Takes the Bus
lessons.summary: A student writes for the school newspaper about a city council candidate who wants better buses and less traffic.
lessons.text:
Lincoln High School News
By Nina Patel

This fall, our city is going to choose 3 new members for the city council. There are 7 candidates. Last week, I met one of the candidates, Ana Ruiz. I chose her because she is the only candidate who comes to work by bus every day.

Ana Ruiz is 45 years old. She is a civil engineer, and she has worked for the city for 15 years. A civil engineer plans roads, bridges and other things that a city needs. When she was a student, she was a sports star at our own school. In 1997, she was the state running champion. Her photo is still on the wall of our sports center, next to the other champions.

"I used to run everywhere," she told me with a smile. "Now I take the bus."

I asked her why the bus was so important to her. "Our city has too much traffic," she said. "Every morning, the traffic on Main Street is terrible. The cars make the air dirty, and people lose hours of their lives. The answer is mass transit: more buses and better buses. Mass transit can move many people easily and for less money."

She showed me some numbers. "There are about 40,000 cars on our roads every day," she said. "That is a conservative estimate. The real number is probably higher. If 1 person in 10 takes the bus, we will have 4,000 fewer cars every day."

I asked, "Will people really use the buses?" "They will, if the buses are fast and easy to use," she said. "Right now, you can't easily get from the north side to the south side of the city. I want to change that."

At the end, I asked the former champion one more question: does she still run? "Of course," she said. "I run to the bus stop every morning!"

The election is on November 4. All 7 candidates will speak in the school hall on October 20.

Questions:
Why did Nina choose to meet Ana Ruiz?
She chose her because Ana is the only candidate who comes to work by bus every day.
What does a civil engineer do?
A civil engineer plans roads, bridges and other things that a city needs.
What was Ana Ruiz in 1997?
She was the state running champion.
What does Ana Ruiz think is the answer to the traffic?
She thinks that the answer is mass transit: more buses and better buses.
Why does she call 40,000 cars a conservative estimate?
She calls it conservative because the real number is probably higher.
